lines.li: [them] Your lamps burn without smoke, and the elders would want to know how.
[us] It's power from the generator, carried along wires.
[them] Then you've tamed a kind of lightning.
[us] Something like that.
[them] My people would say a fire you can't see is a fire you can't trust.
[them] Your healers have medicines that would empty a sickhouse back home.
[us] And yours know plants we've never heard of.
[them,their:tribal] Then trade me a little of yours, and I'll show you the bitter root.
[them] Then let's trade, a little of what you have for a little of what we know.
[us] That sounds fair to me.
[us] How do your people say goodbye to the dead?
[them] We sing them to the fire all night, so the smoke carries the song up.
[us] Ours mostly go into the ground, with a few words said over them.
[them] Then the song stays in the ground with them, and that seems lonely to me.
[us] Maybe we'll borrow one of your songs, next time.
[them] Borrow it, and sing it loud, the dead are hard of hearing.
[them] You have an hour for everything here, even for sleeping.
[us] It keeps things running.
[them] At home the sun and the bells do that, and nobody argues with either.
[us] We argue with ours all the time.
[us] It must be hard, living without the things we have here.
[them,their:tribal] We live with what the land gives, and it gives more than you'd think.
[them,their:medieval] We manage, the way your grandparents managed, I expect.
[them] We manage well enough, and we don't miss what we never had.
[us] I didn't mean it to sound like that.
[them] I know, and I'm not offended, only a little amused.
[them,their:tribal] You have the clever things, but nobody here tans a hide like my people.
[them,their:medieval] You have the clever things, but I'd set our cheese against anything you make.
[them] You have the clever things, but some goods are still best made by hand.
[us] Then let's see what you've brought.
[them] The elders would give a great deal for tools like yours.
[us] We might spare a few, for the right trade.
[them] Then we'll talk, and I'll try not to look too eager.
[them] Do the machines work for you, or do you work for the machines?
[us] Some days it's hard to say.
[them] That's what my grandfather used to say about his ox.
[them] I've heard of places like yours, but I never thought I'd see one this far out.
[us] It took a long time to get here, and a lot of mistakes.
[them] Most of us never get there, mistakes or no.
[them] Everything here happens so quickly, I hardly know where to look.
[us] You get used to it.
[them] I'd rather not, at home a thing takes as long as it takes.
[them] Is it true you can talk to people far away through a box?
[us] It is, if you have the right machine and someone listening at the other end.
[them] Could I talk to my grandmother?
[us] Only if she has a box too.
[them] She has a goat, would that do?
[them] My grandmother used to tell me how her people lived, and it was a lot like this.
[us] Did she miss it?
[them] Every winter, she said, and never once in summer.
[them] You'd get on a lot faster with proper equipment, you know.
[us,tribal] We get on at the pace the land allows.
[us] We get on fine at our own pace.
[them] I meant no offense, only that you'd have more time to rest.
[us] We rest well enough, thank you.
[us] Your people make medicine we can't, I'm told.
[them,their:spacer] We do, and we'd trade some for food grown in real soil.
[them] We do, and we'd trade some for what your fields grow.
[us] Then we'll talk when your traders come by.
[them] You'd have an easier time with a rifle or two, out here.
[us] A bow needs nothing we can't make ourselves.
[them] That's a better answer than I expected.
[them] Your people raised all this with your own hands, didn't they?
[us] Every wall, and most of them twice.
[them] Where I come from, nobody has built a wall by hand in generations.
[us] Then you've been spared a great many sore backs.
[them] The Empire has halls that would astonish you, but none with your view.
[us] We like our view.
[them] As you should, it cannot be bought, and at court that is rare.
[them] Your machines are sturdy, I'll give you that, the kind you fix with a hammer.
[us] We fix everything with a hammer, sooner or later.
[them] Mine need a clean room and a week, so I envy you a little.
[them] Back home, things made by hand like yours fetch a good price.
[us] Then I hope you'll pay a good price for them here.
[them] Let's not get carried away, I have a living to make.
[us] What's it like, where you come from?
[them,their:empire] Ordered, graceful and watched, and one learns to love all three.
[them,their:spacer] Clean, quiet and very well lit, and some days I miss the dirt.
[them,their:industrial] Loud, smoky and full of engines, and I miss it every day.
[them,their:medieval] Walls, bells and markets, and more people in one street than live here.
[them] Busier than here, and not always better.
[us] I'd like to see it one day.
[them] Then I hope you do, I'd show you round.
[them] Who's your lord out here, then?
[us] We answer to the council, and the council answers to us.
[them] That sounds either very wise or very tiring.
[us] Both, most days.
[them] I'll keep what you gave me somewhere people can see it.
[us] It's only a small thing.
[them] Where I'm from, a thing made by someone's hands is never small.
[us] Is it true that where you live the lights never go out?
[them,their:spacer] Never, we have to make our own nights.
[them] Not never, but later than here, and nobody minds.
[us] I'd never sleep.
[them] You'd learn, everybody does.
[them] Your hunters and mine follow the same herds, I think.
[us] Then we should agree whose turn it is.
[them] The elders could settle it, or the herds will settle it for us.
[us] What marks a child grown among your people?
[them] Their first hunt, or their first winter alone with the herds, whichever comes first.
[us] Ours is much the same, though we argue about which counts.
[them] Every tribe argues about that, it's how you know they're a tribe.
[them] Do your folk owe a tithe, or is everything here your own?
[us] Everything we grow is ours, and so is every bad harvest.
[them] Aye, freedom cuts both ways, as my father always said.
[them] Whoever hung your doors knew their trade.
[us] I'll tell them you said so.
[them] Tell them a guild would take them, if they ever tire of you.
[them] What are you paying for fuel out here, if you don't mind me asking?
[us] Mostly sweat, we cut our own.
[them] Smart, the prices back home would make you weep.
[them] Places like ours run on three things, fuel, food and someone who can fix the pump.
[us] And we're always short of the third.
[them] Everyone is, that's why they get paid so well.
[them] It's rare to meet anyone out here who speaks our kind of shop talk.
[us] I've been saving up questions for someone like you.
[them] Then ask, and I'll pretend I know all the answers.
[them] Your colony has the means of a proper house, if not yet the manners.
[us] Manners can be learned.
[them] Indeed, and I would be glad to watch them learned.
[them] You make the same things we make, so I'll have to be clever about what I sell you.
[us] Or you could just be cheap.
[them] Clever is cheaper, for me.
[us] How do your people mark a wedding?
[them,their:tribal] A gift feast, and the whole camp sings until the fire dies.
[them,their:medieval] A feast, a dance, and the bride's family pretending to be poor.
[them,their:empire] A ceremony with every title read aloud, which takes most of the day.
[them,their:spacer] A contract, a toast and a long night nobody writes down.
[them] A party that runs out of drink before it runs out of guests.
[us] It sounds like what we'd do.
[them] People are people, whatever they build with.
